plan_a_advantages: Prioritizes hill work and sustained tempo runs, directly mimicking trail running demands.
Includes a longer, more representative long run (152 minutes) compared to Plan B.
Better prepares the athlete for the specific challenges of climbing and maintaining pace on trails.
plan_b_advantages: Incorporates strength and mobility work, which is beneficial for injury prevention and overall running efficiency.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it directly addresses the demands of trail running – incorporating significant hill work and a longer, sustained tempo run. Plan B, while well-structured, focuses heavily on aerobic threshold work and cross-training, which are important but don't sufficiently build the specific strength and endurance needed for challenging trail terrain. Plan A’s inclusion of hill repeats and a longer tempo run will translate more directly to improved climbing speed and sustained effort, crucial for trail racing. Furthermore, the longer runs in Plan A are more representative of the distances often encountered in trail races.
